text: OXBOW, Sask., June 28, 1923. A cyclone of terrific force swept across the farming district south of town late yesterday afternoon, cutting a path a quarter of a mile wide and some eight miles long. Eyewitnesses describe a black funnel that dipped and rose several times before striking the farm of Mr. Arne Halvorsen, where the house and barn were lifted from their foundations and scattered across the fields. Mrs. Halvorsen and two children took shelter in the root cellar and escaped with bruises. Granaries, machinery and fences were wrecked along the route, and a threshing outfit was found overturned in a coulee. Heavy rain and hail followed the storm.
label: storm

text: Funnel cloud touched down briefly near Carberry, Man., on 4 July 2016; one machine shed destroyed, no injuries. The farmer who owned the shed watched from his kitchen window as the funnel dropped out of a dark wall cloud, threw up a cloud of dust and sheet metal, and pulled back up within seconds. Pieces of the roof were found half a kilometre away in a canola field.
label: storm

text: Hail the size of golf balls pounded the district between Hanna and Youngstown for twenty minutes on the afternoon of August 5, 1957, flattening wheat and barley that was within days of harvest. Adjusters put the loss on some quarters at 100 per cent. Windows were broken on the north side of nearly every farmhouse in the storm's path.
label: storm

text: A weakening hurricane passed just south of Cape Breton on the night of 13 September 1983, bringing gusts of 130 km/h and torrential rain. Trees fell across power lines from Port Hawkesbury to Glace Bay, leaving about 60,000 customers in the dark. Fishing boats broke from their moorings at Louisbourg, shore sheds were swept away, and several roofs were peeled back in Sydney.
label: storm

text: Lightning killed eleven head of cattle sheltering under a lone elm on the Mackay farm near Pictou during a heavy thunderstorm on the 18th. July 1906.
label: storm

text: Box 7, file 3. Eleven photographs taken by a local druggist the morning after the windstorm of 2 August 1952 at Moose Jaw. They show the grandstand at the exhibition grounds folded like a card table, a grain elevator annex with its cupola torn away, and elm trees lying across Main Street with their roots in the air. One print shows a boxcar blown off a siding. A pencilled note says the wind came from the west 'like a freight train' and lasted barely five minutes. Three people were hurt by flying glass.
label: storm

text: Environment Canada has confirmed that an EF1 tornado with estimated maximum winds of 150 km/h touched down near Mitchell, Ont., at about 4:40 p.m. on 22 June 2016. The damage path was roughly 7 km long and up to 200 m wide. Several barns lost their roofs, a silo collapsed, and hundreds of trees were snapped or uprooted. No injuries were reported.
label: storm

text: Hail shredded the tobacco crop around Delhi, Ont., in late July 1961; some growers lost every leaf in the field. The storm came in from Lake Erie at mid-afternoon and lasted barely ten minutes, but the stones, some as big as walnuts, left the plants standing as bare stalks. Kilns stood idle that fall on a dozen farms, and the growers asked the province for relief.
label: storm

text: One of the fiercest gales in the memory of the oldest fishermen struck the south basin of Lake Winnipeg on the 22nd and blew without slackening for thirty hours. At Gimli the waves broke over the breakwater and swept away a row of fish sheds with their nets and gear. Two sailboats were driven ashore near Hnausa and wrecked on the rocks, though their crews scrambled to safety. Several houses along the beach lost their verandahs, and the wind piled the water so high that the lower streets were awash. September 1906.
label: storm

text: Downburst winds estimated at more than 120 km/h tore through the campground at Sandbanks Provincial Park on the evening of 12 August 2002, toppling dozens of large trees onto tents and trailers. Four campers were taken to hospital in Picton; park staff cleared two campground loops overnight.
label: storm

text: Hailstorm at Lacombe, Alta., July 1908. Crops in a strip two miles wide were completely destroyed, and glass was broken in every greenhouse in town.
label: storm

text: SARNIA, Aug. 9, 1955. A brief but violent squall with winds estimated at seventy miles an hour roared across the city shortly after noon today, uprooting shade trees, tearing the roof off a downtown hardware store and toppling a construction crane on the waterfront. Two workmen were injured by falling bricks. Power was off in much of the east end for several hours.
label: storm

text: Severe thunderstorm with 2 cm hail and 90 km/h gusts, Saskatoon, 20 July 2005. Trees down, scattered outages. Several large elms fell across streets in Nutana and City Park, crushing at least three parked cars, and an outdoor stage on the riverbank was blown over minutes after the crowd had been cleared.
label: storm

text: A deep low tracking up the Gulf of St. Lawrence drove a storm surge of about 1.2 metres onto the Northumberland Strait shore on the morning of 29 October 1993, arriving within an hour of high tide. Waves topped the dunes at Cap-Pele and Shediac Bridge, flooding cottages, washing out sections of the shore road and stranding lobster boats on the wharf aprons. Gusts at Moncton reached 110 km/h and power was cut to some 30,000 customers. Provincial emergency officials opened two reception centres, and fire departments in boats helped about 80 cottage owners to safety. Erosion cut the bank back by up to five metres in places.
label: storm

text: Lightning killed a farmer working in his summerfallow near Melfort, Sask., on 6 July 1930. He had stayed on his tractor to finish a round as the thunderstorm came up. His son, working a field away, saw the flash and found him lying beside the machine. The coroner ruled it death by lightning and no inquest was held.
label: storm

text: A tornado touched down on the outskirts of Arthur, Ont., about 6 p.m. on Thursday, May 21, 1959, and travelled northeast for nearly ten miles. Three farm homes were destroyed and a dozen barns flattened; a woman was killed when her kitchen wall collapsed. Neighbours worked through the night with lanterns, searching the rubble and rounding up scattered livestock.
label: storm

text: A southeast windstorm swept Greater Victoria on 22 November 2001, uprooting firs and Garry oaks and dropping them across power lines from Sooke to Sidney. About 70,000 homes were in the dark by evening.
label: storm

text: From the monthly weather summary for Saskatchewan, July 1914: a severe thunderstorm accompanied by heavy hail passed over the districts of Kindersley and Rosetown on the afternoon of the 16th, moving from west to east at a rapid rate. Hailstones were reported as large as hen's eggs and lay to a depth of four inches in places an hour after the storm. Growing grain was beaten into the ground over an estimated 60,000 acres. Several horses were killed in the open, and a man driving a team near Rosetown was badly bruised about the head and shoulders.
label: storm

text: The insurance industry put losses at roughly $30 million after hailstones up to the size of tennis balls fell on Brooks, Alta., for about fifteen minutes on 22 July 2010. Shingles and siding were shredded across most of the town, car windshields were smashed in dealership lots, and skylights at the high school gave way, letting rain pour into classrooms.
label: storm

text: A waterspout came ashore at Wasaga Beach in August 1964, flipping rowboats and tearing the roof from a refreshment stand. Bathers had watched the column of spray twisting over the bay for several minutes and ran for cover when it turned toward the beach. A woman was knocked down by a flying beach umbrella. Once on land the spout weakened and broke up in the pines behind the cottages.
label: storm

text: It was over in less than a minute, but the tornado that crossed the south end of Morden, Man., on the evening of 19 June 2015 left a trail of wreckage nearly four kilometres long. Residents described a deafening roar and hail the size of walnuts just before the funnel touched down near the golf course. It lifted the roof from the curling rink, rolled two semi-trailers onto their sides in an industrial yard and stripped siding from dozens of homes. A transmission tower was bent to the ground, cutting power to the town and several neighbouring municipalities for most of the night. Three people suffered minor injuries. Environment Canada rated the tornado an EF2, with winds estimated at 180 to 200 km/h.
label: storm

text: A thunderstorm with heavy hail passed over the Brandon district on the 11th, causing serious losses to standing wheat. August 1902.
label: storm

text: Letter from the principal, Swift Current Collegiate, to the Department of Education, 14 June 1958: I regret to inform you that Sunday's windstorm carried off most of the roof of our north wing. Rain the same night ruined the library and soaked two classrooms. Pupils have been doubled up in the remaining rooms, and the examinations will be written in the Legion hall.
label: storm

text: A line of severe thunderstorms raced across central Ontario on the afternoon of 2 July 1977, bringing straight-line winds that forecasters later estimated at 130 km/h. Cottage country took the worst of it: on the lakes north of Gravenhurst, boathouses were knocked flat, docks were torn loose and thousands of pines and maples came down across roads and power lines. Two canoeists were rescued after clinging to their overturned canoe on Lake Muskoka for nearly an hour. Ontario Hydro crews needed most of a week to restore power to remote cottages, and the township brought in extra trucks to haul away fallen timber.
label: storm

text: Tornado warning ended 19:45. Damage survey team dispatched to Clinton, Ont., to assess reports of a destroyed hog barn and roof damage on Huron Road. (Storm prediction centre log, 7 August 2006)
label: storm

text: A heavy gale from the northeast swept Bonavista Bay on the 3rd and 4th of October 1910, driving several schooners from their moorings at Greenspond and smashing stages and flakes along the shore. Much of the fall catch of salt fish, spread out to dry, was blown into the sea.
label: storm

text: My father kept a farm diary all his life, and the entry for 30 June 1953 is the longest in the book. 'Hot and close all morning. Big clouds building in the west by 3. Hail started at 4:20, first like peas then like eggs, and the wind came with it. Lost the south quarter of wheat entirely, the oats are flat, every window on the west side is gone. Then a twister went down along the creek a mile east of us, we saw it plain, took Olsen's barn and his new Chev truck. Nobody hurt, thank God. Rain all night.' He replanted nothing that year; it was too late, and the hail insurance paid less than half.
label: storm

text: Microburst damaged hangar roofs at the Abbotsford airport on 2 August 1996; two light aircraft were flipped on the apron. Staff in the tower reported a sudden gust above 100 km/h as a rain shaft collapsed directly over the field. No one was hurt, but flights were held for an hour while crews cleared sheet metal from the taxiways.
label: storm

text: Tropical storm remnants brought sustained winds of 70 km/h and gusts to 100 km/h across the Avalon Peninsula on 12 September 1986, along with 90 mm of rain. Several power poles snapped in Mount Pearl, a section of roof was torn from a shopping centre in St. John's, and waves damaged the breakwater at Bay Bulls. About 40,000 customers lost power.
label: storm

text: WIND DOES HEAVY DAMAGE. A violent windstorm visited Lethbridge Saturday night, tearing down signs, telephone wires and chimneys all over the city. The new hospital lost part of its roof, and a large frame livery barn on Round Street was blown down, killing two horses. July 1910.
label: storm

text: The so-called dry thunderstorm that crossed the Okanagan on 8 August 1985 produced more than 2,000 lightning strikes in four hours but almost no rain. Outflow winds of 90 km/h raised clouds of dust along the highway and snapped branches in the orchards above Kelowna. Lightning blew out the wiring of a house in Rutland and killed a horse in a field near Westbank.
label: storm

text: Thunderstorm, Fredericton, 23 July 1935: torrential rain and lightning; a barn was struck at Lincoln, and the electric light was off in the city for two hours.
label: storm

text: FORECASTER'S NOTE, 11 June 1987. The supercell that tracked from near Olds to east of Three Hills between 1500 and 1800 MDT produced at least two brief tornadoes, large hail up to 6 cm and wind gusts estimated near 120 km/h. Damage reports include a destroyed Quonset, a mobile home rolled onto its roof (two occupants injured) and extensive crop damage. Radar showed a hook echo for about 40 minutes.
label: storm

text: The wind came up so suddenly over Lake of the Woods that afternoon in August 1947 that most of the fishing boats were caught in open water. Waves of six feet and more were reported off Kenora, and a launch was swamped near Coney Island, though its four passengers were picked up by a passing tug. On shore, the gale took down dozens of pines on the islands and smashed the windows of the Harbourfront hotel. A guide at Sioux Narrows said he had never seen the lake so white.
label: storm

text: Hail, 3 cm, reported by a spotter at Brandon, 17:05 CDT, 14 June 2000.
label: storm

text: An intense line of thunderstorms with winds near 100 km/h swept through the Fraser Valley on the evening of 23 June 1972, knocking down orchards near Chilliwack and blowing several hop kilns off their footings. Two people were struck by lightning on a golf course in Langley; one died.
label: storm

text: Tornado at Bowmanville, Ont., 6 May 1934. The storm unroofed several houses on the north side of town, tore down the fair grounds fence and wrecked a large implement shed. Reports say the funnel was seen crossing the highway west of town before it lifted.
label: storm

text: Post-tropical storm. Western Newfoundland, 24 October 2007. Peak gust 148 km/h at Wreckhouse; tractor-trailers held at Port aux Basques. Roofs damaged in Stephenville, power off to 15,000 customers. Storm surge of 0.9 m overtopped the causeway at Burnt Islands.
label: storm

text: A summer storm with exceptionally high winds blew down the wireless mast at Cape Race and stripped the roofs from several houses at Portugal Cove South, August 1912.
label: storm

text: YARMOUTH, Aug. 26, 1924. The tail of a West Indian hurricane struck the western end of the province last night with a fury not seen in years. Plate glass windows on Main Street were blown in, chimneys toppled, and the steeple of the church at Hebron was carried away. In the harbour the wind drove a number of fishing vessels hard against the wharves, and the tide, pushed far above its usual mark, flooded the lower floors of the warehouses along Water Street. Telegraph lines are down in every direction and news from the outlying villages is slow to come in.
label: storm
